topic: Count singular some and the indefinite article
claim: Some and anyn occur with count singular heads “as in [30]” and may therefore contrast with the indefinite article.
evidence_summary: [30] is the exclamatory use (Those are SOME elephants!), non-quantitative and plural in [30a]. [29] is “Vague count singular use”, where some “is in competition with the indefinite article a”.
finding: Change [30] to [29], with medium confidence. [30b] SOME hotel that was! is count singular, so [30] partly fits. But [30] is the exclamatory use, which the paragraph’s second reason, the restriction to quantitative uses, excludes, while [29] is the use described as competing with a.
inference: Does the cited example show competition with a?

evidence.passage: §7.5, p. 384. “are also found, albeit less frequently, with count singular heads, as in [30], for example.”
evidence.example: Page 380 [29] and the comment that follows it.
evidence.note: Local source (working note, unpublished draft or local copy); not online.
